annotation.summary_en: A driver stranded by his broken-down Lada asks several passersby for mechanical help, only for the final technician's question about a 'secret' to lead to an awkward confession.
annotation.summary_detailed_en: The sketch is set on a tree-lined roadside where a man stands by his broken-down white VAZ-2106 (Lada) with the hood open. He is on the phone with a friend named Ash, explaining that he will be late for a birthday party because the car, which he claims belongs to his nephew, has stalled. First, a man in a striped shirt stops to help. The driver pretends he usually drives 'firm' cars and isn't used to Soviet models. They discuss the fuel pump (benzinanasos), but despite 'fiddling' with it while the driver tries to start the engine, the car remains dead. Next, a more formal man offers help, suggesting the battery is dead, but he also leaves when he cannot find a 'secret' (a hidden anti-theft switch). Finally, an older man in a flat cap arrives, offering a convoluted explanation about the 'zaklatno' getting wet. He tells the driver to pump the pedals while he works. When the old man asks if the driver has a 'secret', the driver shamefully confesses his actual life secret: he sleeps with his mother-in-law. The old man yells in frustration, realizing the driver misunderstood the automotive term for a personal confession.
